reviews.title: This app is single-handedly helping me get through college
reviews.text: I am someone with a pretty severe case of ADHD. I have tried many methods that were just not effective for me to focus on my assignments because as an online student I need my phone (my biggest distraction) to do things for my schooling such as sharing files back and forth and using authentication apps. But focus friend makes it so the apps that usually distract me without me realizing are not an option for me to use, and it allows me to set a timer for a designated amount of work with breaks in between. Whenever I need to sit down and do assignments I immediately turn on the app and I have noticed a huge increase in not only my productivity but also in my endurance to handle the work. And the small reward of decorating my bean’s space gives me some external motivation to get my work done when I don’t feel in the mood. It is one of the few tools I have used that doesn’t get me trapped in a shame spiral when I am implementing it. I recommend this app to anyone and everyone I possibly can. 10/10

reviews.title: Evaluation of Focus Friend for Adolescents
reviews.text:
Focus Friend by Hank Green is a 4.5-star app for adolescents because it provides a safe, fun, expressive, and engaging way for teens to develop their concentration and time-management skills. Focus Friend’s system is very conducive and attractive to adolescents as it uses a gamified system that is focused on rewards rather than punishments and consequences. When users complete a focus session, they are rewarded with socks, allowing them to trade them for goods. Because adolescents have a heightened sensitivity to rewards due to their increase in dopamine receptors, rewards are a much stronger behavioral motivator as opposed to punishments. Moreover, because the premise of the app is imaginative and its aesthetic is very cute, the app and its rewards will likely be more attractive to its adolescent users. Another way in which Focus Friend is well suited to the adolescent brain is there is no shaming language or punishments when a user quits the focus session. When this happens, the bean simply says “It’s okay! We tried!” This is important because adolescents are less sensitive to negative consequences and punishments in this phase of development. Therefore, how the app is currently gamified is well suited to garnering adolescent engagement. 
In addition, Focus Friend then uses that engagement to help promote healthy executive function skills during a time of heightened neuroplasticity for adolescent users. For many adolescents, success in social, academic, and personal pursuits depends on their ability to delay gratification. However, this is becoming increasingly difficult, as a 2022 study found that 54% of teens reported it would be difficult for them to give up social media. Moreover, 46% of teens say they use the internet almost constantly. Given these findings, it is not surprising that a 2026 study found that 29% of teens felt their productivity has been negatively impacted by TikTok. Because the adolescent brain undergoes a heightened period of neuroplasticity, making it especially sensitive to environmental factors, it is important to help teens develop self-regulation skills regarding their technology. By incentivizing teens to not use their phones via focus sessions, users can develop a stronger, life-long ability to delay gratification. Though this is the point of a focus timer, Focus Friend also does this by not having ads and not collecting any user data that can be used to entice further screen time. These features make Focus Friend an app that can teach valuable life skills for teens. 
Focus Friend also provides adolescents with a safe and fun environment to experiment with and express their identities. Researchers have found that adolescents use avatars in online games to explore both their real and idealized versions of themselves. However, with this comes the risk of avatars invoking feelings of low self-esteem if teens fixate on the ways in which their avatar meets ideal beauty standards that they do not. What Focus Friend does so well is it provides an outlet for users to express themselves without reinforcing stereotypes and beauty standards. While users can express their individuality through their bean’s accessories and room décor, because the avatar is a bean and not a person, there is likely greater detachment and less of a risk of internalizing comparisons to one’s bean. Focus Friend also caters to adolescents’ identity exploration by allowing users to change their bean’s name at any time. When users are prompted to name their bean, the app says “Uhh…Who am I? You can change this later. I am still figuring out who I am and who I want to be.” The fluidity with which users can change their avatar and the largely a-gender nature of the bean is important for adolescents, who are focused on identity formation and experimentation in order to develop a sense of self that incorporates all facets of who they are. This can be especially important for adolescents exploring their gender identity, as the bean and its variety of room décor and accessory choices are a departure from traditional gender norms. Research has found that for transgender and gender non-conforming adolescents, avatars can be an important part of exploring and affirming their gender identity. Online environments can also be a safer space to express their gender identity for adolescents living in an environment that is not accepting of who they are. 
Though Focus Friend has many benefits in what it can offer to adolescent users, there are some drawbacks that must be considered when rating. One consideration is that Focus Friend is not compatible on computers, where adolescents can still be distracted by screens. Though popular apps like TikTok and Snapchat are not well suited to or compatible on desktop platforms, video and streaming services like YouTube and Netflix can still be accessed. This is especially important to address since Pew Research found that 1 in 5 teens report being on YouTube almost constantly. Moreover, teens are more likely to complete their schoolwork on a computer as opposed to their phone, so prioritizing concentration and focus on this device is very important. So, while Focus Friend is a great tool for managing mobile screen time, it fails to account for the easily accessible and distractible nature of computers. Focus Friend’s other main drawback is the lack of in-app accessibility features. For example, there is no voiceover that can read the onscreen text for users who are visually impaired. Moreover, during focus sessions, apps that help users manage their disabilities (e.g., diabetes management apps) cannot be accessed without quitting the session or paying for a subscription. Additionally, all avatars appear to be able-bodied, which does not provide representation for those with disabilities who require mobility aides like a wheelchair or cane and who would like their avatar to have the same. 
With the app’s flaws in mind, this is overall $a great app for teen users.

reviews.title: Where has this bean all my life…
reviews.text:
I cannot explain just how much this has helped me. You can absolutely tell that the developers understand ADHD in such a fundamental way that so many productivity apps just don’t.

Task paralysis is the worst. Things I need to do, and even things I *want* to do? Can’t start them, or finish them. There’s so much shame built around it, especially living in a fast paced productive world that definitely wasn’t built with neurodivergency in mind.

But with this app, I just feel so much less pressured. It’s not about how many tasks i’ve finished, it’s about how much you can get done in the time that you give the little bean to knit his socks!

What’s really insane to me is how well this app is executed. Like I said, the developers clearly understand ADHD. This app combines different helpful strategies for task paralysis. The body-doubling strategy is obvious, of doing a task alongside someone, since it’s exactly what this is. The bean is your friend, and when he needs to focus, you can focus alongside him. It’s super wholesome. And of course, the reward system is great. The bean makes socks I can use to buy him furniture and accessories. It’s so cute!!
Speaking of cuteness, the art style is adorable too. And I love how there’s a few references to media that i’m actually interested in. I was not expecting to see Miku and Madoka Magica… And the bean going, “Where you bean, loca?” made me laugh, I love it!!!

If there’s any chance the developer(s) see this, thank you so much for this gem. I would give 10 stars if I could!! :)

reviews.title: So helpful and cute <3!
reviews.text:
Focus friend is THE app if you get super distracted (like me lol). I always multitask which usually is fine, but doing homework always takes me like two hours because I start going on other apps or literally just walk around. Whether you have adhd, add, or just get distracted, this app is perfect for you! 

In terms of helpful, You can do a regular timer where it can help you keep track of time, but if you have a screen addiction problem, then you can choose deep focus mode: it blocks all other apps except focus friend. Yes, you can get distracted irl like me, but it still helps for staying on task. 

In terms of the cuteness and overall aesthetic, this app also attracts people like me who need help focusing but also want the cuteness. You get a bean that crochets when you set a timer, and it makes socks which you can use to buy furniture. Like isn’t that just adorable!? There are different skins (maybe you could add some more because honestly they look kinda…not cute…but that’s imo) and even different rooms to decorate, plus lots of options for color and the aesthetic of the furniture.

I do think that they could make the furniture less expensive, because it might take awhile to do all the rooms. The app interface could also be improved, as sometimes the app looks like it was only made for a phone screen (like the focus tracker words go off screen) and other times only for iPad.

Overall this app is great~ I totally understand how this got an editors choice <3 Keep it up I love this app tysm!
